title: IoT reading ingestor with a JSON telemetry logger
name: Sensor reading ingestor

locateQuestion.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code records structured log events? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
locateQuestion.explanation: failure() logs the error as { ...err }. An Error's name, message and stack are not own enumerable properties, so the spread copies nothing for a plain Error and the log line contains "error": {}. Every flush failure is logged without its cause, which makes outages of the time-series store very hard to diagnose. It should copy the fields explicitly, e.g. { name: err.name, message: err.message, stack: err.stack }.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A caller passes data { level: "debug", service: "x" } to info(). What do the level and service fields of the emitted line contain?
choices: "debug" and "x", because data is spread after base
"info" and the logger's configured service, because they are written after the spread
The call throws because level is reserved
choiceQuestions.explanation: out() spreads base and data first and then sets service, level and event, so the logger's own values overwrite caller-supplied keys. Nothing validates or rejects reserved keys.

choiceQuestions.prompt: A gateway sends 10 readings, 3 of which have value NaN. What does accept() do?
choices: Rejects the whole batch and returns 0
Buffers 7, logs one warn line with dropped 3 and received 10, and returns 7
Buffers 7 and logs a warn line per dropped reading
choiceQuestions.explanation: Number.isFinite(NaN) is false, so those 3 are skipped and counted; the other 7 are pushed. After the loop a single readings.dropped warn is emitted with the counts, and the return is readings.length - dropped = 7.

choiceQuestions.prompt: writeBatch rejects during flush(). What happens to the batch that was being written?
choices: It is put back at the front of the buffer so a later flush retries it
It is discarded and only counted in the log line
It is moved to the end of the buffer behind newer readings
It stays out of the buffer until flushing is reset
choiceQuestions.explanation: The catch calls this.buffer.unshift(...batch), restoring the readings at the front ahead of anything accepted meanwhile, and finally resets flushing so the next flush can retry. It is not discarded or appended at the end.
